eva_acme: Hi team — after the model migration yesterday our embeddings index suddenly returns 1536-d vectors instead of 768. We pin to a model in the console (customer-managed pin). We started seeing search regressions and a lot of mismatches. sample request_id: req_0a9f2c. Any idea?

jen_support: Sorry you're hitting this, @eva_acme. Can you paste a minimal request/response (no PII) and confirm the pinned model slug you set in the console? Also how many documents are affected roughly?

eva_acme: We pinned to `rw-embed-sm-2024` (console shows pinned). Affected ~120k vectors. Minimal curl we used:```bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-embed-sm-2023","input":"test"}'
```
The response vector length is 1536. We expected 768.

jen_support: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) do you have any app-layer caching/edge proxies? 2) Are you calling the exact model slug as pinned (console pin vs request param mismatch can cause routing).

eva_acme: No caching on our side. Console shows pin to `rw-embed-sm-2024` actually (I typed from memory earlier). But the request body uses `rw-embed-sm-2023` because our infra sets that value. We thought pinning in console would override.

arjun_eng: Looping in infra. Quick hypothesis: if the backend fallback logic changed during the migration, requests specifying older slugs might be routed to a newer family that has a different vector size. Repro-ing locally now.

deploy-bot: deploy event: model-registry:migrate: roll-forward 2024-05-10T03:12:01Z by infra-release

taylor_sre: Noted. @arjun_eng if repro works, let's check routing logs and model manifest mapping (alias -> concrete revision). Also check whether pinned allocations were reconciled post-migration.

arjun_eng: Repro steps I ran: 1) hit embeddings endpoint with `model=rw-embed-sm-2023` 2) capture accept headers and response. Sample response header: `x-model: rw-embed-sm-2024-rev3 (family: rw-embed-sm, dims:1536)` Body trimmed: `{ "embedding": [ ...1536 floats... ] }`. So the backend is returning a 1536-d vector while the request used the older slug.

arjun_eng: Digging into model-registry: looks like during the migration we updated the alias mappings so old slugs now map to new default revisions unless the customer pinned a concrete revision id. The console UI 'pin' stored the alias-level pin, but the routing layer prefers the request param override in a few code paths — and there's a bug where alias pins were not enforced for pinned customers when the alias changed families. In short: alias pin != revision pin in current flow.

jen_support: That's rough. Is there a quick mitigation we can recommend to the customer?

arjun_eng: Immediate workarounds: 1) Instruct customer to set `model_version` (concrete revision id) in the request (we can provide the exact revision id for their previous model) OR 2) In console, update the pin to the exact revision instead of alias. I'll fetch the prior revision id from registry.

taylor_sre: Also adding a temporary safeguard in routing: for pinned accounts, don't remap alias -> new family automatically until reconciliation completes. I'll open a hotfix ticket.

arjun_eng: For @eva_acme your previous revision id appears to be `rw-embed-sm-2023-rev12` which is 768 dims. You can try this curl:```bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-embed-sm-2023","model_version":"rw-embed-sm-2023-rev12","input":"test"}'
```
That should return 768. If it does, we can schedule a bulk reindex or we can revert the alias mapping for your org.

eva_acme: Tested the exact revision id, confirmed 768 vectors now. Huge relief.

jen_support: Great. We're going to: 1) apply a routing guard for pinned orgs (short-lived hotfix) 2) follow up with a console change to make pin-to-revision the default for customers using pins 3) offer credits and help reindex the affected vectors.

arjun_eng: Root cause summary for the ticket: model-registry alias remap during migration caused old alias slugs to point to new family revisions; console stored alias-level pins which did not guarantee routing to the older revision in some code paths. Fixes: mapping reconciliation + UI change + routing guard.

taylor_sre: Hotfix PR opened: "do-not-remap-pinned-orgs" -> will gate by org metadata flag while we reconcile. Link in internal ticket.

deploy-bot: incident-tracker: created incident INC-2024-1987 (severity: low)

jen_support: @eva_acme we've scheduled a follow-up to: share the list of affected indices, provide a one-off re-ingest script, and apply a billing credit for compute spent on mismatched vectors. We'll keep you updated in-thread. Apologies again.

eva_acme: Thanks everyone — patch worked, and the reindex plan sounds good. Please let me know ETA and any temporary rate limits while you run fixes.

arjun_eng: ETA for hotfix rollout: ~2 hours for canary, full rollout in 6 hours pending telemetry. We'll DM with any rate-limit windows.

jen_support: I'll create KB article summarizing the symptom, repro, and the concrete revision workaround. We'll link that here when ready. :thumbsup:

taylor_sre: Postmortem TODOs: - KB + KB link - Console change to surface "pin to revision" - E2E test to assert pinned orgs always resolve to pinned revision - Billing/credits follow-up

jen_support: Closing note: if anyone else sees customers with similar symptoms, tell them to try sending `model_version` with the known good revision until console UI update lands.

eva_acme: Copy. Thanks again, team.
